votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 40 of 2022, recognizing December 1st as World AIDS Day in Salt Lake City.
votes.description: A joint ceremonial resolution with Mayor Mendenhall to officially recognize December 1st as World AIDS Day in Salt Lake City.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer items B-1 through B-4 to a future Consent Agenda for action.
votes.description: Closes the public hearing on four grant applications (Reconnecting Communities Pilot, Homeless Shelter Cities Mitigation, Plug-In Electric Vehicle Make-Ready, and Urban Sustainability Directors Network) and refers them to a future consent agenda for formal action.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 75 of 2022, amending the zoning of the property at approximately 856 West 1300 South from R-1/5,000 to FB-UN1 with a requirement that the petitioner enter a development agreement with specified conditions.
votes.description: Rezones a single-family residential parcel at 856 West 1300 South to Form Based Urban Neighborhood District (FB-UN1) with a development agreement requiring residential use only, maximum 2.5 stories/30 feet height, at least one parking space per unit, no more than 60% lot coverage, and at least three bedrooms per dwelling unit.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 41 of 2022, authorizing the donation of certain City computers to benefit disadvantaged communities and low to moderate income families through a digital donation program.
votes.description: Authorizes the donation of 146 surplus City computers to local nonprofits for distribution to community members in need, with 25 allocated to Youth and Family Services.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 42 of 2022, accepting the special election results of the Salt Lake City Parks, Trails, and Open Space Bond.
votes.description: Accepts the certified canvassed results of the Special Bond Election held November 8, 2022, approving an $85 million general obligation bond for investments in parks, trails, and open spaces across all Council Districts.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 76 of 2022, approving temporary zoning regulations authorizing a temporary increase in overnight capacity at the Youth Homeless Resource Center at 888 South 400 West.
votes.description: Enacts temporary zoning regulations allowing the Volunteers of America Youth Resource Center to increase maximum capacity by up to 10 individuals, expiring April 15, 2023.

Approves the full consent agenda including setting a public hearing date for the Library Budget Amendment No. 1, Grant Holding Account Items (Batch No. 5) for FY2022-23, and four Disciplinary Appeals Hearing Officer appointments (Kirsten R. Allen, Brandon T. Crowther, Clinton Drake, and Bryan M. Scott).
